readerTitle: Did the 'only 3 slots left' line really work?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (유리창 청소 업체, 기장 대행 회사) + 실제 연구 (Lewis & Rao 2015, 광고 효과 측정의 어려움)
insight: 매출이 움직였을 때 '무엇이 효과를 냈나'보다 '그때 무엇이 함께 바뀌었나'를 먼저 묻는다.
misconception: 매출이 오른 달에 바꾼 심리 기법 하나가 그 상승을 만든 원인이다.

sources.text: Lewis, R. A., & Rao, J. M. (2015). The Unfavorable Economics of Measuring the Returns to Advertising. Quarterly Journal of Economics, 130(4), 1941–1973.
교란 변수(confounder)와 다중 원인: 통계·연구방법론의 표준 개념
유리창 청소 업체와 기장 대행 회사의 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 가상 수치 계산: 올해 2월 55건 → 3월 77건 = +40% (22 ÷ 55). 작년 2월 50건 → 3월 72건 = +44% (22 ÷ 50). 카드 1~3의 숫자가 서로 맞는지 다시 확인하세요.
Lewis & Rao(2015): 미국 대형 소매·금융 회사의 대규모 온라인 광고 실험 다수를 분석했고, 개인 매출의 변동이 광고 효과보다 훨씬 커서 매우 큰 실험으로도 수익성을 신뢰성 있게 측정하기 어렵다는 결론입니다. 실험 수(약 25개)와 표본 규모는 카드에 구체 숫자로 쓰지 않았습니다. 게시 전 원문으로 요지를 다시 확인하세요.
기장 대행 사례의 '연말에 도움을 찾는 고객이 많다'는 일반적 설명으로만 썼습니다. 특정 국가의 세무 일정이나 통계는 넣지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Did the 'only 3 slots left' line really work?
body: A small window-cleaning company adds one line to its booking page: *Only 3 slots left this week.*
The next month, bookings are up 40%. The owner tells every business friend she has: scarcity works. Put it on everything.
She may be right. But the number she is looking at can't tell her that yet.

image.label: Booking page with a small 'only 3 slots left' banner
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 휴대폰 화면 속 청소 예약 페이지에 작은 빨간 배너 "Only 3 slots left this week". 화면 옆에 위로 솟은 막대그래프와 자랑스러워하는 사장님 캐릭터. 실제 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Bookings jumped. What do you conclude?
body: You're the owner. Bookings went from 55 in February to 77 in March, the month the scarcity line went up.
What's your next move?

options.text: Scarcity works. Add the line to every service and every ad
options.feedback: Fast and confident. But if something else drove March, you'll spread a tactic that may do little, and you'll stop looking for the real cause.

options.text: First list everything else that changed in March
options.feedback: It costs an hour and protects you from crediting the wrong thing. The next card shows what that list turns up.

options.text: Remove the line in April and see if bookings drop
options.feedback: Testing is the right instinct. But April has its own weather, season and word of mouth, so one month on and one month off still mixes causes.

cards.title: Last spring did the same thing.
body: Last year, with no scarcity line, bookings went from 50 in February to 72 in March. That's a 44% jump.
March is when people notice dirty windows. That same month, a happy customer posted in a neighborhood group, and a rival raised prices.

image.label: Last spring did the same thing.
image.brief: Labeled HTML chart from the lesson numbers

cards.title: Many causes, one number
body: Sales are the sum of **many causes acting at once**: season, need, price, trust, reviews, how fast you reply, what rivals do. When a tactic changes at the same time as other things, the sales number can't tell you which one did the work.
The hidden extra causes are called **confounders**. The scarcity line may have helped a little, a lot or not at all. March alone can't say.
cards.softwareNote: A product launch, a pricing page change and a newsletter mention often land in the same week, and dashboards hand the credit to whichever one touched the user last. A/B tests help because both versions run at the same time, so season and press hit both equally.

cards.title: Even huge experiments struggle to hear the signal.
body: Economists Randall Lewis and Justin Rao studied large online ad experiments run by big US companies. Their finding: what each person buys swings so much from week to week that even experiments with very large audiences often couldn't reliably tell whether a campaign paid off.
The effect of any single push is quiet. The everyday noise in sales is loud.
If careful tests with huge samples struggle, one good month at a small business is a whisper.

image.label: A small signal wave buried inside a large noisy wave
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 크게 출렁이는 회색 파도("Normal ups and downs") 안에 작은 주황색 물결("Effect of one tactic")이 겨우 보임. 돋보기로 작은 물결을 찾는 손. 간결한 플랫 스타일.

cards.title: Nudges sit on top of bigger drivers.
body: Most customers decide on a few big things first:
list: **Price:** is it fair next to the alternatives?
**Trust:** do they believe you'll do a good job?
**Ease:** can they book or buy without hassle?
cards.callout: Scarcity, social proof and clever framing can tip a close decision. They rarely create demand that isn't there. And the same goes for bad months: one slow month is rarely one mistake.

cards.title: Don't swing to "nothing can be known."
body: Many causes doesn't mean no causes. A few cheap habits get you most of the way: compare with the same period last year, change one thing at a time, and run old and new side by side, by alternating weeks or customers.
Keep a simple log of what changed and when. It turns guessing into checking.
Match the effort to the stakes. A free, reversible tweak doesn't need proof. Rebuilding your whole sales process does.

cards.title: Now it's a bookkeeping firm.
body: Your firm does bookkeeping for small businesses. In October you redesigned proposals to offer three packages instead of one quote. You won 5 of the next 6 deals.
Many owners look for help before year-end. A partner wants to rewrite the whole sales script around the new proposal. What do you do?

options.text: Roll it out everywhere. Five of six is a clear win
options.feedback: You move fast, but six deals in your busiest season can't separate the proposal from timing, referrals or deal size. A big rewrite rests on a small, mixed signal.

options.text: Keep using it, but alternate old and new proposals for similar deals and compare in a few months
options.feedback: You keep a promising idea working while the season, referrals and deal size hit both versions alike. It's slower, but the rewrite will rest on evidence.

options.text: Ignore it. Six deals mean nothing
options.feedback: Healthy doubt, but you throw away a possibly useful idea. Small samples call for a fair test, not a shrug.

cards.title: When sales move, ask what else moved.
body: Sales have many causes at once. A tactic only earns credit after you rule out the season, the price, the word of mouth and the rivals that changed alongside it.
**Try it today:** pick the last change you credited for a good month. Write down three other things that changed in that same month.
